question: Does the exact positive-coupling global U turn down on a fixed finite grid, as predicted by the two-state strong-coupling limit?
enumerations: one exhaustive 2^25 pass per geometry with the existing rollback topology backend; no Monte Carlo
root: unique zero of mean of separately normalized q means
root_bracket: h_lo=0, h_hi=1, double h_hi until Q>0; FKG implies uniqueness
thermal_variable: h at fixed m; its common Jacobian cancels in U
source_in_h_chart: -g; common homogeneous density reparametrization preserves the entire U(t) curve
preexisting_reference: results/p337-closed-source-n25/latest.json; U(0)>0 and dU_dt(0)>0; do not rerun that calculation
decision: any dU_dt/A enclosure strictly below zero certifies a downturn; positive initial derivative and smooth positive-t root then imply at least one intervening maximum
stop: score the four fixed multipliers once, publish all values; if no negative derivative is resolved, stop without extending the grid
scope: finite-volume named-source model; not a continuum exponent, thermodynamic phase transition, or independent random evidence
